# DocVQA Skill

## Visual Evidence Discipline
- Read the document carefully before answering.
- Prefer the smallest exact text span that answers the question.
- When several nearby strings look similar, use the surrounding labels or layout to identify the entry that best matches the question.
- For questions asking for a value tied to a named table column, list row, grid coordinate, or contact field, first match the exact identifier and field label from the question to the same row/entry and contact block, then read the requested value.
- If similar values are nearby, reject a value from an adjacent row, a different contact field (for example, telephone versus fax), or a secondary office or person block unless the question asks for that secondary entry.
- Return only the verified value, without an explanation.

## Exact Answer Discipline
- Copy names, numbers, and dates exactly from the document whenever possible.
- Prefer direct extraction over paraphrase.
- Return one selected exact numeric or named span as the final answer, not multiple encodings of the same value.
- When the question already names the field or attribute it asks for (for example, a quantity of a named substance, an arrival or departure time, a designation, a nationality, or a state), return only that entry's value, ending at the value's edge. Do not repeat the field name, row label, column header, or the question's quoted substance, product, or attribute wording that located the entry, even if printed beside the value; treat such appended label text as extra answer content. Preserve the full requested value when its own components carry meaning: keep multiword names, name suffixes, printed parenthetical abbreviations, and other printed components belonging to the selected name; keep the printed unit or representation attached to the selected value; and keep quotation marks or punctuation only when they delimit the requested answer itself (for example, a quoted tagline). Apply these boundaries and the existing exact-copy, spacing, punctuation, unit, and no-alternate-encoding rules to the retained value only. Where existing guidance does not specify whether adjacent printed label text belongs to the answer, this scope rule governs.
- For questions asking which brand, company, service, or product is advertised or named, identify the distinctive name that answers the question. If the selected span also contains the question's own generic category wording plus a merely descriptive corporate or geographic extension, return the distinctive name and omit only that category wording and descriptive extension, unless the question asks for the full legal or company name or the extension is needed to distinguish the entity. Do not truncate a multiword proper name merely because it is long; keep titles, initials, suffixes, parenthetical abbreviations, and other printed components that identify the requested person or organization.
- When a requested amount or name appears in more than one form, such as a symbol, written-out words, a currency conversion, or a parenthetical abbreviation, identify the field, cell, or entry that answers the question and return only the value exactly as printed there.
- For a numeric answer, determine the exact printed value in the selected cell or entry before deciding whether to include a unit symbol; a percent sign, currency symbol, or unit shown only in the question wording or a column heading is contextual and is not appended to a cell value that prints only the number.
- If the selected value itself prints a percent sign, currency symbol, comma grouping, decimal fraction, or other unit or representation, keep that printed form exactly and do not strip or normalize it merely because another form appears elsewhere.
- Do not append restatements, conversions, or alternate forms from elsewhere unless the question explicitly asks for them. If the question asks for a specific representation or unit, use that representation from the document.
- Keep a parenthetical abbreviation only when it is printed as part of the selected name. Copy the chosen span's internal spacing and punctuation exactly as printed, including whether a space appears before a parenthetical abbreviation; do not insert or remove a space to match conventional prose.
- When the requested answer is itself a quoted title, tagline, or quoted expression, or contains a quoted word as part of a title, keep the quotation marks but transcribe opening and closing marks as plain ASCII double quotes (") rather than typographic curly quotes (“ ”), unless the question explicitly asks to reproduce the document's typographic punctuation or the quoted text is a literal code/markup string. For these delimiting quotation marks only, this transcription convention governs over the general instruction to copy punctuation exactly as printed; the general exact-copy preference continues to apply to the internal punctuation, spacing, and words inside the quotation marks.
- Preserve the quoted wording exactly, including capitalization, internal spacing, and all non-quote punctuation; do not strip the quotation marks, add quotation marks where they are not part of the requested answer, or split a coordinated pair of quoted expressions requested by a plural question.
- Limit this quote-mark convention to quotation marks that delimit requested answer text; keep apostrophes, parenthetical abbreviations, percent signs, currency symbols, commas, decimals, and other printed punctuation unchanged, and retain the complete requested span when it is a full sentence or title.
- When multiple printed encodings exist, choose the answering entry's exact printed value as the selected span rather than treating every alternate encoding as a separate candidate.
- Before finalizing, compare the answer against nearby alternatives and keep the best-supported exact span.
